description: This IEEE DataPort dataset holds satellite image chips of individual buildings in the Greater Houston area after Hurricane Harvey in 2017, each labelled as flooded or damaged, or as undamaged, for training building damage classifiers. It accompanies the paper by Quoc Dung Cao and Youngjun Choe, first posted on arXiv in July 2018 and published in Natural Hazards in 2020, which extracts square windows around known building coordinates from post-hurricane imagery, uses damage labels from a volunteer crowdsourcing project, and reports over 97% accuracy with a custom convolutional neural network. The zip holds four folders: training data with 5,000 images per class, validation data with 1,000 per class, an unbalanced test set of 8,000 damaged and 1,000 undamaged images, and a balanced test set of 1,000 per class; the class is given by the folder name. Coverage: the Houston area after Hurricane Harvey, August 2017. Access: one 63.05 MB zip of JPEG images on IEEE DataPort, DOI 10.21227/sdad-1e56, issued 2018-12-13; open access but downloading needs a free IEEE account. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution; free. Caveats: labels come from volunteers, the chips carry no coordinates in the file names described, and the damage class merges flooding with structural damage. Simulation uses are training and benchmarking remote-sensing damage detection that feeds post-event exposure and loss estimates. Related records: the Ian-BD aerial damage dataset and the Harris County building population estimates; the services piece holds xBD.
